full_judgment: 61. Mr Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate for the convict appellant-condemned prisoner has placed the argument before us that since the occurrence of calling out and commission of murder took place in broad day light and there were so many inhabitants in the locality in adjoining place of occurrence, there must be eye-witnesses, but surprisingly, no independent eye-witness is available in this case. He submits that the prosecution examined only 17 witnesses out of 29 cited witnesses of the charge-sheet Therefore, non-examination of some material witnesses gives rise to adverse presumption in favour of the defence under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and therefore, it casts serious doubt as to the genuine version of the prosecution case. In this respect, we find from the record that the accused is a well identified criminal having other murder cases against him and it is evident from the impugned judgment that he was a listed terrorist in the locality. Reportedly, he is also a convict in another murder case. Naturally, it is not expected that the independent neighbouring witness, even if any, would come to depose against him in the present law and order situation prevailing in the country, particularly when the accused was absconder for a long time and there was fear in the mind of witnesses during investigation period Moreover, there is no evidence before us to say that any outsider and man of the locality had seen the occurrence of committing murder or witnessed calling and taking away of the deceased by the accused. The defence side has not been able to point out any such material witness, who was competent to depose about actual events relating to the occurrence.
